subject: Environment
description: Stratospheric vs tropospheric ozone, ODS, Montreal Protocol, Kigali amendment

questions.stem: The ozone layer is mainly located in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The 'good' ozone layer sits in the lower stratosphere — roughly 15-35 km above sea level, with peak concentration ~25 km. It absorbs 97-99% of harmful UV-B radiation. Atmosphere layers (bottom up) — Troposphere (0-12 km), Stratosphere (12-50 km, contains ozone layer), Mesosphere (50-85 km), Thermosphere (85-600 km), Exosphere. Tropospheric ozone (near ground) — different role: a pollutant and greenhouse gas.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.explanation: Ozone (O₃) — three oxygen atoms; an allotropic form of oxygen alongside O₂ (the air we breathe). Bluish, pungent gas. Formed in stratosphere by UV splitting O₂ → 2O, then O + O₂ → O₃ (Chapman cycle, 1930). Half-life depends on temperature/pressure but in stratosphere remains balanced naturally. Major absorber of UV-B (280-315 nm), preventing skin cancer / cataracts / DNA damage on Earth's surface.

questions.stem: The international treaty for phasing out ozone-depleting substances is the:
questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer — signed 16 September 1987 (a date now observed as World Ozone Day), came into force 1 Jan 1989. Universally ratified — 198 parties. Phases out CFCs, HCFCs, halons, methyl bromide. Considered the most successful environmental treaty — ozone hole healing observed; full recovery projected by 2066 (Antarctic). Kyoto/Paris target greenhouse gases; Stockholm targets persistent organic pollutants.

questions.stem: The 2016 Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol added phase-down obligations for:
questions.explanation: Kigali Amendment (15 Oct 2016, in force 1 Jan 2019) — adds HFCs to the list. HFCs replaced CFCs/HCFCs as refrigerants but turned out to be potent greenhouse gases (1000s× more warming than CO₂). India ratified in Sep 2021. India's HFC schedule: freeze 2028, 10% reduction by 2032, 80% reduction by 2047. Could prevent ~0.5 °C of additional warming by 2100.

options.option_text: Beneficial gas that protects from UV
Secondary pollutant + greenhouse gas formed from NOx + VOCs in sunlight

questions.explanation: Tropospheric ozone — 'bad' ozone — formed when nitrogen oxides (vehicle/industrial exhaust) and volatile organic compounds react in sunlight (photochemical smog, peaks on hot afternoons). Causes lung damage, asthma flare-ups, crop yield loss. Also a short-lived greenhouse gas (3rd biggest after CO₂ and CH₄ globally). Stratospheric ozone protects life; tropospheric ozone harms it. Same molecule, different altitude → opposite role.

questions.stem: The 'ozone hole' is most pronounced over which region of Earth?
questions.explanation: First reported by British Antarctic Survey scientists Farman, Gardiner, Shanklin in Nature, 1985. The hole appears each austral spring (Sep-Nov) over Antarctica because polar stratospheric clouds (forming below −78 °C in winter) provide surfaces for chlorine activation; sunlight returning in spring then triggers ozone destruction. Largest extent recorded — 2000 (~30 million km²). Recovery underway; Antarctic ozone projected to return to 1980 levels by ~2066.

questions.stem: Ozone column thickness is measured in:
questions.explanation: Dobson Unit (DU) — named after British meteorologist G.M.B. Dobson (1920s). 1 DU = ozone column 0.01 mm thick at standard temperature/pressure. Global average ~300 DU; values below 220 DU define the 'ozone hole'. Lowest readings — Antarctica in spring, ~100 DU. Measurement instruments — Dobson spectrophotometer; satellite — TOMS, OMI on Aura satellite. India contributes via Maitri / Bharati Antarctic stations.
